strings.name: Viet Thanh Nguyen
strings.role: Novelist · Critic and writer in residence
strings.summary: Nguyen came to the United States as a child refugee and developed a career across scholarship and creative writing. The Sympathizer reconsidered the Vietnam War and its aftermath through a divided narrator, winning the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. His fiction, memoir and criticism ask who controls stories of war and exile. After years of teaching, he became USC's writer in residence.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Reexamines war, refugees and memory through The Sympathizer and criticism, expanding Vietnamese experience in international literature.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Ban Mê Thuột, South Vietnam, now Buôn Ma Thuột, Vietnam; raised in the United States.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Bachelor's degrees in English and ethnic studies and a 1997 English PhD from UC Berkeley.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Retelling war experience
strings.highlights.h1.text: The Sympathizer uses espionage fiction to examine allegiance, memory and American imaginings of the Vietnam War.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Across fiction and criticism
strings.highlights.h2.text: Brings refugee experience to stories, memoir and arguments about war memory and the humanities.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discussed writing and the humanities
strings.timeline.t1.text: A long interview addressed To Save and to Destroy, ethnic studies and narrative power.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Published his Norton Lectures
strings.timeline.t2.text: To Save and to Destroy: Writing as an Other examined literature's capacity both to liberate and to exclude.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Published A Man of Two Faces
strings.timeline.t3.text: The memoir revisited refugee childhood, family labor and contradictions of American identity.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Published The Committed
strings.timeline.t4.text: The Sympathizer's sequel moved its characters to Paris to explore colonial history and political loyalties.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Published refugee stories
strings.timeline.t5.text: The Refugees appeared; he also received a MacArthur fellowship that year.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Won the Pulitzer for Fiction
strings.timeline.t6.text: The Sympathizer, published in 2015, won; Nothing Ever Dies examined war memory in the same year.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Completed his PhD and began teaching
strings.timeline.t7.text: After his Berkeley doctorate, joined USC, combining literary scholarship with creative work.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Arrived as a refugee with his family
strings.timeline.t8.text: Initially resettled in Pennsylvania before moving to San Jose, California.
